March 2023: Kentucky Power filed its 2022 integrated resource plan with the Public Service Commission, and the preferred plan adds 480 MW of new gas combustion turbines in 2029. This is the first document that announces the unit. https://psc.ky.gov/pscecf/2023-00092/sebishop@aep.com/03202023030104/KPCO_2022_IRP_Volume_A-Public.pdf

Kentucky Power told the Public Service Commission in October 2026 that it dropped its plan for a 450 MW combustion turbine (case 2026-00103, withdrawn by the order of October 29, 2026) and will instead seek approval for a 760 MW combined cycle plant in Lawrence County with a planned in-service date of March 31, 2031 (new case 2026-00324, notice of intent filed October 30, 2026). https://psc.ky.gov/pscscf/2026%20Cases/2026-00103//20261029_PSC_ORDER.pdf

Status Detail.note:
Open the plan at https://psc.ky.gov/pscecf/2023-00092/sebishop@aep.com/03202023030104/KPCO_2022_IRP_Volume_A-Public.pdf. The commission filing path and the docket listing for case 2023-00092 give the filing date of March 20, 2023. The preferred plan adds 480 MW of new gas combustion turbines in 2029 as the Mitchell coal unit leaves the portfolio. That dates the announced step to March 2023.

The Kentucky Public Service Commission order of October 29, 2026 and the commission staff memorandum of the October 8, 2026 informal conference both say Kentucky Power replaced its 450 MW turbine plan with a 760 MW combined cycle plan. The notice of intent in case 2026-00324 names a natural gas-fired combined cycle plant in Lawrence County. The status stays announced because no application has been filed yet.

milestones.note: Kentucky Power filed its 2022 integrated resource plan on March 20, 2023. Its preferred plan adds 480 MW of gas combustion turbines in 2029.

units.notes: The unit stays announced. Kentucky Power now plans a 760 MW combined cycle plant in Lawrence County, so the placeholder is raised as a question.

qa.question: Should this placeholder be folded into Kentucky Power's Lawrence County combined cycle project?
qa.finding: The 2022 resource plan (https://psc.ky.gov/pscecf/2023-00092/sebishop@aep.com/03202023030104/KPCO_2022_IRP_Volume_A-Public.pdf) adds 480 MW of gas turbines in 2029. Kentucky Power later planned a 450 MW turbine (case 2026-00103), withdrew it (https://psc.ky.gov/pscscf/2026%20Cases/2026-00103//20261029_PSC_ORDER.pdf), and told commission staff it will file for a 760 MW combined cycle plant with a planned in-service date of March 31, 2031 (https://psc.ky.gov/pscscf/2026%20cases/2026-00103//20261012_PSC%20Letter%20Filing%20Informal%20Conference%20Memorandum%20and%20Attendance%20List%20into%20the%20Record.pdf). Case 2026-00324 (https://psc.ky.gov/pscscf/2026%20cases/2026-00324//20261030_Kentucky%20Power%20Company%20Notice%20of%20Intent%20and%20Election.pdf) is the notice of intent for a natural gas-fired combined cycle plant in Lawrence County.
qa.recommendation: Keep this record as announced for now. Once Kentucky Power files the application, rename or merge it into the sited Lawrence County project and change capacity to 760 MW and start year to 2031, or ask the project manager whether to do that now.
qa.note: The 2026-00324 application itself was not yet posted on the commission site when I looked. Only the notice of intent, the acknowledgment letter and a motion to intervene were. The site within Lawrence County is not named in what I could read. The brief suggests Big Sandy, but I found no document that says so. The 760 MW figure and the 2031 date come from commission staff's memorandum of what Kentucky Power said, not from an application. A new record for the sited plant is left for the reviewer because no site, owner entity or turbine model is yet documented.

qa.question: Should the placeholder's point near Pikeville be moved to Lawrence County?
qa.finding: GEM's point is 37.46994, -82.53118, which is at Pikeville in Pike County, and no document sites this unit. Kentucky Power's 2026 notice of intent places the combined cycle plant in Lawrence County, and the brief points to Big Sandy, but no source I read gives an address or coordinates.
qa.recommendation: Leave the point and the approximate accuracy as they are until Kentucky Power's application names the site.
qa.note: No address, parcel or coordinates were published in the documents I could read, so the geocoding and satellite steps could not be run. City and county stay blank for the same reason.

qa.question: Is any turbine model or backup power use stated for this unit?
qa.finding: The 2022 plan and the 2026 commission documents do not name a turbine make or model, and none describes the unit as backup power.
qa.recommendation: Leave the turbine model as not found and Backup Power as no until the certificate application is posted.
qa.note: I read the commission order, the staff memorandum and the notice of intent. I did not read the full 2022 plan beyond the capacity and year.

source_log.note: Staff memo of the informal conference.
Case filings page listed only the notice, acknowledgment letter and a motion to intervene.

Reopened on November 5, 2026. It still lists only the notice of intent, an acknowledgment letter, a read-first file and a motion to intervene, so there is no application, site, operator or turbine model yet. The notice of intent names only Lawrence County.
